Broadly, focus is on the ongoing energy supply disruptions in the Middle East and stalled talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz to maritime traffic.
That has pushed oil prices higher and helped global bond yields reach fresh multi-year highs on Tuesday, as markets price in further tightening from global central banks.

Banks (.SX7P) tend to benefit from higher yields but are actually the weak spot in Europe, hindered by comments from Bank of America CEO Brian Moynihan after he said sales and trading revenue will be flat in the third quarter.
Aerospace and defence stocks (.SXPARO) are the rare pocket of strength, helped by reports that Japan is eyeing a boost to defence spending and that the Pentagon was looking to replenish stockpiles.
